unreach.why: The requirement's comparison set is "any game previously uploaded to the Website", and that catalogue is not in this repository and cannot be enumerated from it. Session 2 established this by search rather than assumption: reports/qa/compliance_register/walk_shards/W12.md:279-281 states "No proof is possible from this repository alone ... the comparison set is 'any game previously uploaded to the Website', which is not in the tree and cannot be enumerated from it", and the only committed clearance artefact, docs/records/trademark/2026-07-15/SEARCH_LOG.md, expressly declines to clear even the NAME against "prefix, part-word, phonetic or visual-similarity conflicts" (quoted at W12.md:203-204). No gate reading this tree can compare our title against titles it cannot see. What would close it is a dated, captured originality assessment against the platform's published catalogue, of the kind docs/records/trademark/ already does for the name — an owner-side capture pass, not a CI instrument. PRECISION ABOUT WHICH HALF: the clause's SECOND half, "blocks submitting a second near-identical build of our own", IS mechanically reachable and is noted below as a cheap rider on the provenance manifest gate; it is not enough on its own to call this requirement covered, because the operative demand is distinctness from the platform's catalogue.

The requirement IS a third party's inspection verdict, not a property of an artefact. approval_guidelines.md:18, quoted: "Our team will inspect the game for functionality, clarity, communication, and technical performance. These factors determine the suitability of your game for publication." Nothing in the repository decomposes those four axes into checkable obligations, and W07.md:30-51 refused to invent a decomposition for exactly that reason. The ten wired browser legs at .github/workflows/checks.yml:601-629 defend fragments of "technical performance" and "clarity", but each asserts one rendering or animation property and no union of them adds up to a reviewer's judgement; building a gate named after the requirement would be a proxy wearing the requirement's name, which is convention (l.6)'s wrongly-solved failure. The row is also UNKNOWN rather than NO_PROOF because the clarity axis carries an open confirmed defect, KNOWN(C-01) at reports/qa/stream_test/KNOWN_OPEN.md:52, `GameGrid.svelte:499`, `DROP_H = 520`, the reel window bare for 312 of 412 pixels on every drop. That is a fix, not a proof mechanism.

approval_guidelines_game_quality_rankings.md:26 bands the build on "considerable creativity or originality plus strong development quality". Creativity and originality are not measurable properties of a tree. W21.md:137-152 established that QUALITY_CHARTER.md section 2.2's seven properties are all FINISH properties and none speaks to creativity, and that the only repository statement about star bands at all is a target at COMPLIANCE_WATCH.md:212. A gate that counted gates and printed a star rating would be circular. Note that the failure mode here is the opposite of REQ-042's: polish is explicitly ALLOWED to trail at this band, so the open Q-26/Q-27/Q-34 rows do not bear on it.

Original IP only.', so a gate asserting the line is PRESENT would enforce a breach of the project's own rule, and a gate asserting it is ABSENT would enforce a position nobody has ruled. The requirement is an outcome awarded by a third party. Ratings remain hidden until all three are submitted. / Average >= 1 star -> Game is approved for production. / Average < 1 star -> Game is rejected." rejected.name: cross-os-cross-browser-matrix
rejected.why: DIAGNOSIS, grounded in what the ten legs actually are. checks.yml:598-630 lists layout fit, contrast, splash calm, turbo intensity, paytable card fill, scrim coverage, win count-up steady, max-win hold, bet selector, preview server. The mechanism's own negative control demands the browser wall-clock stay inside the measured 2.9-to-4.6-minute envelope while multiplying ten legs by three engines and two operating systems. Those two requirements cannot both hold. A defensible version names the SUBSET of legs whose assertion is engine-independent (network, DOM presence, request shape) and adds webkit for those only, with the pixel gates explicitly excluded and that exclusion recorded.

A workflow run only exists because GitHub already holds the commit; actions/checkout@v4 creates a remote-tracking ref for whatever it checked out (on pull_request, refs/remotes/pull/N/merge), so `git branch -r --contains HEAD` is non-empty by construction. The refusal can never fire. (2) 'tracked frontend/ files differ from HEAD' is computed by `git status --porcelain -z` (:120-123) over a checkout that actions/checkout has just created from a clean object store. frontendDirty is empty by construction. Wiring this produces two assertions that print PASS in every possible CI run — the exact 'script that prints PASS' failure convention (p) names, reproduced at the wiring step rather than in the predicate. The proposal's own seed_form correctly identifies that the existing selfTest() (:167-183, verified: five hand-made fact objects plus four livePart cases) tests only the predicate, then prescribes a throwaway real git repository — but a throwaway repository proves the plumbing works, not that CI can ever present the facts that trip it.
